rationale: Acceptance did not run (no story/spec artifact), so business-criteria coverage is unavailable and confidence is capped at low. Edge-case lens raised 4 candidates; 3 verified as real, reachable defects — buildServerConfig() never receives isCatalogRef so a catalogue-restricted server's pre-existing custom config keeps resubmitting unchanged on every save (critical), a matching MCPConfigSection display bug shows stale custom JSON under a 'Global' label (major), and processBackendError's new string-details branch leaves a dangling colon on empty strings (major) — while the mcpMode.ts null-configs concern was dismissed as unreachable (its only call site always passes an array). Standards audit is clean: commit-format and security pass; code-quality has no guide (na, not a gap).

standards_review.notes: All 5 commit subjects in range match EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence format with real ticket id, capitalized first word, no trailing period.
No code-quality guide found at .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md and no ArtifactRef passed for code_quality; absent standard, not a gap.

security-patterns.md checklist checked against changed files: no unsafe sinks, redirects, postMessage, env/secret reads, or nosonar additions; the isCatalogRef/isMCPRestrictedMode logic is UI-affordance only, no concrete security defect found.

findings.title: Read-only field can show stale config, not catalog
findings.problem: The read-only textarea's displayed value only checks `!useCustomConfig`, not `isCatalogRef` — when isCatalogRef is true but useCustomConfig is still true (a custom copy saved before restricted mode was enabled), the box renders the stale custom JSON via `field.value` instead of catalogConfig.
findings.impact: The field is disabled and labeled '- Global' (governance-enforced) but visibly displays outdated custom configuration, misleading an admin about what configuration will actually be used once governance is enforced.
findings.recommendation: Include isCatalogRef in the display condition, e.g. `(isCatalogRef || !useCustomConfig) && hasCatalogReference && catalogConfig ? JSON.stringify(catalogConfig, null, 2) : field.value`.

findings.title: Custom config not cleared for catalogue-restricted servers
findings.problem: buildServerConfig() is called as `buildServerConfig(values, mcpServer?.mcp_config_id)` and never receives isCatalogRef; it unconditionally sets `mcpServer.use_custom_config = values.useCustomConfig` and keeps `mcpServer.config = config` whenever `values.useCustomConfig` is true, with no override for the catalogue-restricted case. formHelpers.test.ts has no test covering isCatalogRef at all.
findings.impact: When editing a pre-existing custom-config catalogue server after restricted mode is turned on, the Global/Custom toggle is hidden and the JSON field is disabled, but every save still resubmits `use_custom_config: true` plus the old custom JSON unchanged — even for edits to unrelated fields — so the frontend never actually enforces catalogue-only config at the data layer, only in the display.
findings.recommendation: Pass isCatalogRef into buildServerConfig (or apply the same override where it is called in MCPToolkitForm/index.tsx) and force `use_custom_config: false` / `config: undefined` whenever isCatalogRef is true, mirroring what MCPConfigSection already enforces visually.

findings.title: Empty details string leaves dangling colon
findings.problem: processBackendError appends `: ${error.details}` whenever `typeof error.details === 'string'`, with no check that it is non-empty, so an empty-string `details` still enters the branch. No test in backendErrorHandler.test.ts covers an empty-string details value.
findings.impact: The general error text shown to the user ends with a dangling 'message: ' instead of a clean message for the one input shape this branch was added to handle correctly.
findings.recommendation: Guard the branch with a non-empty check, e.g. `typeof error.details === 'string' && error.details`.
